links.comparator_used: Zero-shot baseline (no retrieval) on llama3.2:1b and llama3.2:3b
links.outcome: Category-level diagnostic accuracy and high-risk recall on 24-case DSM-Bench-24 vignettes
links.effect: RAG improved 1B accuracy (75.0%→79.2%) but degraded 3B accuracy (83.3%→75.0%); high-risk recall dropped to 0/2 under both RAG configurations
links.tradeoff: High-risk recall fell to 0/2 under RAG even where accuracy improved (new safety failure mode); mechanism unclear since retrieved DSM criteria for BPD mention self-harm
links.quote: RAG improved the 1B model (75.0%→79.2%) but degraded the 3B model (83.3%→75.0%); LoRA fine-tuning left Qwen's accuracy unchanged (70.8%→70.8%, same count, different cases).

links.comparator_used: Zero-shot baseline of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (off-the-shelf, no fine-tuning)
links.outcome: Category-level diagnostic accuracy and high-risk recall on 24-case DSM-Bench-24 vignettes
links.effect: Accuracy unchanged (70.8%→70.8%, same count, different cases); high-risk recall dropped to 0/2 after LoRA fine-tuning
links.tradeoff: Safety degradation: high-risk recall fell to 0/2, traced to a training data flaw that labeled the BPD example's risk tier as moderate rather than high, teaching the wrong association
links.quote: For fine-tuning we trace this to a specific, disclosed methodological flaw: our training data labeled the Borderline Personality Disorder training example's risk tier as moderate rather than high, teaching the model exactly the wrong association.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to existing LLM
